claim: For every integer \(r\ge2\), let \(X_{r,a,b}=\mathbb P(1^r,a,b)\) with \(1\le a\le b\), and let \(\iota_{\mathrm{Pic}}(X)=[\mathrm{Cl}(X):\mathrm{Pic}(X)]\). Then \(\iota_{\mathrm{Pic}}(X)=\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\). Among the canonical members, \(\iota_{\mathrm{Pic}}(X)\le(2r-1)(3r-1)\), with equality uniquely at \((a,b)=(2r-1,3r-1)\). Among the terminal members, for \(r=2\) the maximum is \(6\), attained uniquely at \((a,b)=(2,3)\); for every \(r\ge3\), \(\iota_{\mathrm{Pic}}(X)\le(2r-3)(3r-4)\), with equality uniquely at \((a,b)=(2r-3,3r-4)\).

correctness.rationale: For well-formed weighted projective space, the hyperplane Weil class maps to a generator of each local class group, so its Cartier multiples are exactly the multiples of the least common multiple of the weights. The two-heavy Reid--Tai calculation gives the canonical triangle \(0\le d\le r, 1\le a\le r+d\) and terminal triangle \(0\le d\le r-1, 1\le a\le r+d-1\). A complete boundary case split then proves the stated maxima and uniqueness; the bundled exact checker independently verifies all age conditions and lcm extrema through \(r=60\).

value.rationale: The Picard index is a structural measure of the gap between Weil and Cartier divisor theory and equals the minimal weighted degree at which the hyperplane class becomes a line bundle. Determining its worst possible size under canonical or terminal singularities gives an exact all-dimensional obstruction bound with unique extremizers, rather than a routine evaluation for a fixed weight vector.
